Thanks Vanessa — great summary. Quick answers and a few follow-ups inline: 

1) SDK languages: Confirm Node (backend service) and Python (analytics/ETL). We may later add a small Java microservice.

2) Auth: API keys are fine for PoC. For production we will require mTLS + enterprise KMS integration. Can you outline your mTLS support and cert rotation process?

3) Routing: region-based routing is a hard requirement (EU residency for some customers), plus model-family fallback is nice to have (we can accept degraded quality for cost savings on non-critical flows).

4) Structured output: prefer function-calling / strict JSON schema for the assistant when we’re getting structured responses (e.g., product IDs, actions). For freeform suggestions, plain chat is OK. We’ll need examples.

5) Embeddings/reranker: We generally use 768–1024 dims today. Latency target for reranker end-to-end is ~150ms for top-10 re-rank on 100 candidates. We use a managed vector DB (we’re evaluating Pinecone).

6) Tokenization & code: yes, code blobs are common (up to ~12k tokens). Important to understand chunking + how stop tokens interact with streaming.

Attached: Synthex_Security_Q.pdf — it’s our initial security questionnaire; can you confirm where to upload evidence (SOC2, data-residency statements, encryption docs)?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice@synthex.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Synthex integration — SDK/auth & response-schema follow-ups

Hi Alice / Vanessa — quick technical notes ahead of Wednesday. I’ll bring a short demo. Answers below to help Synthex prep.

Auth & environments:
- PoC: API keys (short-lived) are the fastest path. Redwood SDKs support environment variables + Vault integrations.
- Prod: we support mutual TLS (mTLS) and customer-managed KMS (HSM/KMS) for key material. Cert rotation is handled via our control plane; customers can push cert bundles or use ACME-style automation in private deployments.

Routing & fallbacks:
- We support policy-based routing: route by region, latency SLO, or model family. Policies are JSON configs you can store in our Console.
- Fallback: automatic model demotion to a quantized variant (lower-cost, lower-accuracy) if the preferred pool is saturated.

Chat vs completions / function-calling:
- Use chat for multi-turn stateful interactions and when you need function-calling / structured output. Chat APIs preserve messages and role tokens which simplifies context-windowing.
- Completions (single-shot) are OK for templated prompts or one-off generation.
- For structured output, we recommend JSON schema validation + our function-calling wrapper (we return a single JSON blob as a dedicated field). Example (simplified):

Request: POST /v1/chat/completions
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>
Body (partial): {
  "model": "redwood-chat-3b",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Get product info"}],
  "functions": [{"name":"get_product","parameters": {"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"}}}}],
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "stop": ["\\n\\n"],
  "stream": false
}

Response (skeleton): {
  "id": "chatcmpl-xyz",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "choices": [{"message": {"role":"assistant","content": null, "function_call": {"name":"get_product","arguments": "{\"id\":\"sku-123\"}"}}}],
  "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 120, "completion_tokens": 20}
}

Tokenization & long code blobs:
- We use the same tokenization family as the model (tiktoken-like). For large code assets (~12k tokens) we recommend chunking with overlap and using embeddings for retrieval + a short completion for synthesis.
- Stop tokens: If you supply stop sequences, the model will emit until it sees that sequence. With streaming enabled, that may mean you get partial content up until the stop; client should handle back-pressure and assemble chunks.

Streaming semantics:
- Streaming is chunked deltas. Each event includes role and partial content deltas; the final event closes the stream with usage/ids. We support Server-Sent Events (SSE) and HTTP chunked streaming.
- Important: with function-calling, streaming may delay the function_call field until the call is complete. For deterministic function-calling we recommend non-streamed or structured finalization step.

Embeddings & reranker:
- Embedding dims vary by model; many open models are 1024–1536. If you are on a 768-dim runtime we’ll recommend re-indexing.
- Reranker pattern: 1) produce semantic-recall via ANN (FAISS/Pinecone) with ~100 candidates; 2) run a cross-encoder or lightweight pointwise scorer for top-10 to re-rank. This balances recall + rerank latency.

Sample Node snippet (streaming chat, simplified):
const res = await redwood.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood-chat-3b',
  messages: [{role:'user',content:'Summarize the code snippet'}],
  stream: true
});
res.on('data', chunk => { /* chunk.delta appended to buffer */ });
res.on('end', () => { /* finalization, usage */ });

Cost/latency note:
- Streaming reduces perceived latency for the user but can add overhead server-side if you also do cross-encoder reranking during the same flow. Consider async rerank (background) for non-blocking UX.

Looking forward to Wed 11:00 PT — I’ll bring the Node example + a small reranker demo.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
